subject.title: macOS: Gateway daemon PATH excludes user bin dirs (nix, bun, local, etc.)

question: Should macOS managed Gateway services keep the current canonical system PATH, or should OpenClaw support user-bin/Nix/Bun paths through a default change or explicit opt-in?
rationale: The source change is straightforward, but the behavior controls daemon command-resolution trust and could make user-writable package-manager paths part of managed service execution.

options.title: Add an explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep the default canonical PATH and add a maintainer-approved service PATH opt-in with doctor, docs, and tests for fresh install and reinstall behavior.

options.title: Change the macOS default
options.body: Include Darwin user-bin directories by default and own the compatibility and security impact for all managed macOS installs.

options.title: Keep current policy
options.body: Document that managed macOS services intentionally omit user-bin directories and direct exec-only use cases to `tools.exec.pathPrepend` or absolute commands.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit opt-in
recommendation.body: Keep the default canonical PATH and add a maintainer-approved service PATH opt-in with doctor, docs, and tests for fresh install and reinstall behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice cuts across Gateway service setup, doctor policy, and daemon security defaults, where the history points most strongly to steipete as the routing owner.
